subject: maths
title: Chapter 7 · Test 2
summary: Chapter 7 · Test 2: a 15-question check on angles, congruence, enlargements and similar triangles.
body:
Test 2 checks the whole of Chapter 7: angle rules with parallel lines, triangles and polygons; congruent triangles and the SSS, SAS, AAS and RHS tests; enlargements and scale factors; similar triangles; and real-world problems such as shadows, mirrors, ramps and rivers.

Allow about 25 minutes, with no notes. A calculator is allowed for the measurement problems, but try to work exactly where you can. Many questions have a diagram — read the markings carefully (ticks for equal sides, arcs for equal angles, arrows for parallel lines). Give every answer in the units asked for.

questions.prompt: Three angles meet at a point, as shown in the diagram. Find x.
questions.explanation: Angles at a point add to 360°, so x = 360° − 110° − 95° = 155°. 205° is the sum of the known angles.
steps: Step 1: angles at a point add to 360°.

mistakes.A: Step 2: 205° is 110° + 95°, the two known angles. Subtract them from 360°.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you only subtracted 110°. Subtract both known angles from 360°.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you only subtracted 95°. Subtract both known angles from 360°.

questions.diagram_alt: Three rays from one point making angles of 110°, 95° and x around the point

questions.explanation: The vertices match in order: K↔X, L↔Y, M↔Z, so ∠M = ∠Z. ∠X matches ∠K instead.
steps: Step 1: match the letters in order: K↔X, L↔Y, M↔Z.

mistakes.A: Step 1: X is the 1st letter of XYZ, so it matches K, not M.
mistakes.B: Step 1: Y is the 2nd letter of XYZ, so it matches L, not M.
mistakes.C: Step 1: ∠K is in the same triangle as ∠M. The matching angle must come from △XYZ.

questions.prompt: After an enlargement, a 3 cm side of a shape becomes 12 cm long. What is the scale factor?
questions.explanation: Scale factor = new ÷ old = 12 ÷ 3 = 4. 9 is the difference, which is not how scale factors work.
steps: Step 1: scale factor = new length ÷ old length.

mistakes.B: Step 1: 9 is the difference 12 − 3. A scale factor is found by dividing.
mistakes.C: Step 1: you divided old by new. Scale factor = new ÷ old = 12 ÷ 3.
mistakes.D: Step 1: you multiplied 12 by 3. Divide the new length by the old length.

questions.prompt: △ABC ||| △DEF, with a scale factor of 3 from △ABC to △DEF. DE = 12 cm. Find AB.
questions.explanation: AB matches DE, and △ABC is the smaller triangle, so AB = 12 ÷ 3 = 4 cm. 36 cm multiplies the wrong way.
steps: Step 1: AB matches DE, and △DEF is 3 times as big.

mistakes.A: Step 2: you multiplied by 3. △ABC is the smaller triangle, so divide DE by 3.
mistakes.B: Step 2: you subtracted 3. Divide by the scale factor instead.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you added 3. △ABC is smaller, so divide by 3.

questions.prompt: The diagram shows two parallel lines and a transversal, with one angle of 124°. Find x.
questions.explanation: x and 124° are both between the parallel lines on the same side of the transversal (a C shape), so they add to 180°: x = 56°. Setting them equal treats them as alternate angles.
steps: Step 1: x and 124° are co-interior angles (C shape), so they add to 180°.

mistakes.A: Step 1: x and the 124° angle are co-interior (same side, between the lines), so they add to 180°, not equal.
mistakes.B: Step 2: you subtracted from 360°. Co-interior angles add to 180°.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you subtracted 90°. Co-interior angles add to 180°.

questions.diagram_alt: Two parallel lines cut by a transversal. At the top crossing the angle below the line on the right is 124°. At the bottom crossing x is the angle above the line on the right

questions.prompt: △ABC ≅ △DEF, as shown in the diagram. ∠A = 58° and ∠B = 47°. Find y = ∠F.
questions.explanation: ∠F matches ∠C = 180° − 58° − 47° = 75°. Choosing 47° matches F with B instead of C.

mistakes.A: Step 1: F matches C, not B. ∠B = 47° matches ∠E.
mistakes.C: Step 1: F matches C, not A. ∠A = 58° matches ∠D.
mistakes.D: Step 2: 105° is 58° + 47°. Subtract this from 180° to get ∠C.

questions.diagram_alt: Triangle ABC with angle A = 58° and angle B = 47°, and a congruent triangle DEF (flipped) with angle F marked y. AB and DE carry matching ticks

questions.prompt: Triangle PQR in the diagram is enlarged from the origin O by scale factor ½. What are the coordinates of P′?
questions.explanation: P(6, 4) is 6 right and 4 up from O. Halving gives 3 right and 2 up, so P′ = (3, 2). Multiplying by 2 gives an enlargement, not a reduction.
steps: Step 1: from O, P(6, 4) is 6 right and 4 up.

mistakes.B: Step 2: you multiplied by 2. A scale factor of ½ halves the distances from O.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you subtracted ½ from each coordinate. Multiply by ½ instead.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you halved only the x-coordinate. Halve both.

questions.diagram_alt: A grid with the origin O marked and triangle PQR with P(6, 4), Q(8, 4) and R(6, 2)

questions.prompt: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 6 cm and 8 cm. Which triangle is similar to it?
questions.explanation: 7.5 ÷ 5 = 9 ÷ 6 = 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5, so all three ratios match (SSS). Adding the same amount to each side changes the shape.
steps: Step 1: divide each side by the matching side of the original (smallest with smallest).
Step 2: 7.5 ÷ 5 = 1.5, 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5 and 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5 — all equal, so it is similar.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you added 2 cm to each side. Similar triangles need the same multiplier: 7 ÷ 5 and 8 ÷ 6 differ.
mistakes.B: Step 2: the first two sides double, but 14 ÷ 8 is not 2. All three ratios must match.
mistakes.D: Step 1: you added 1 cm to each side. Check the ratios: 6 ÷ 5 and 7 ÷ 6 differ.

questions.prompt: A ramp starts at A. A 0.8 m vertical post stands 3 m from A, and the ramp ends above D, 9 m from A (see the diagram). Find the height h at the end of the ramp.
questions.explanation: The triangles share ∠A and have right angles, so k = 9 ÷ 3 = 3 and h = 0.8 × 3 = 2.4 m. 3 m is the scale factor, not the height.
steps: Step 1: △ABC ||| △ADE (shared angle, right angles), so k = 9 ÷ 3 = 3.

mistakes.A: Step 2: you added 6 m (the extra distance along the ground). Multiply by the scale factor instead.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you used the scale factor upside down. The end of the ramp is higher than the post.
mistakes.D: Step 2: 3 is the scale factor 9 ÷ 3. Multiply the post height by it.

questions.diagram_alt: A ramp from A rising to E above D. A vertical post BC of 0.8 m stands 3 m from A, AD = 9 m, and the height DE is h

questions.prompt: Find x in the hexagon in the diagram.
questions.explanation: The angles add to 720°: 120 + 130 + 110 + x + x + x + 30 = 720, so 3x + 390 = 720 and x = 110. 140 is the size of (x + 30)°, not x.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you used 540° as the angle sum. A hexagon's angles add to (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°.
mistakes.B: Step 2: you left out the + 30 from the angle (x + 30)°. Include it before solving.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 140° is the angle (x + 30)°. The question asks for x.

questions.diagram_alt: Hexagon ABCDEF with angles A = 120°, B = 130°, C = 110°, D = x°, E = x° and F = (x + 30)°

questions.prompt: In kite ABCD in the diagram, AB = AD and CB = CD, and the diagonal AC is drawn. Which statement is correct?

options.D: The triangles are not congruent because only two pairs of sides are marked

questions.explanation: AB = AD and CB = CD (given), and AC is common: three pairs of sides, so SSS. Corresponding angles then give ∠BAC = ∠DAC. The common side is the "hidden" third pair.
steps: Step 1: AB = AD, CB = CD (given) and AC = AC (common side).
Step 2: three pairs of equal sides: △ABC ≅ △ADC (SSS), so the corresponding angles ∠BAC and ∠DAC are equal.

mistakes.B: Step 2: no angle is given, so SAS cannot be used. Three pairs of equal sides is SSS.
mistakes.C: Step 2: no right angle is marked, so RHS cannot be used.
mistakes.D: Step 1: AC is a common side, which gives the third pair of equal sides.

questions.diagram_alt: Kite ABCD with diagonal AC. AB and AD have one tick; CB and CD have two ticks

questions.prompt: In the diagram, DE ∥ BC, AD = 8 cm, AE = 6 cm and EC = 3 cm. Find DB.
questions.explanation: AC = 9 cm, so k = AC ÷ AE = 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5. AB = 8 × 1.5 = 12 cm, so DB = 12 − 8 = 4 cm. 12 cm is the whole side, not DB.

mistakes.A: Step 3: 12 cm is the whole side AB. Subtract AD to find DB.
mistakes.B: Step 2: you multiplied 8 by 6 ÷ 3. AC = 6 + 3 = 9 cm matches AE = 6 cm, so the scale factor is 9 ÷ 6.
mistakes.D: Step 2: you subtracted 3 from 8. Lengths in similar triangles are found with a ratio.

questions.diagram_alt: Triangle ABC with DE parallel to BC. AD = 8 cm, AE = 6 cm, EC = 3 cm and DB is marked with a question mark

questions.prompt: A ladder rests on the ground, just touches the top of a 1.5 m fence and leans on a wall (see the diagram). The foot of the ladder is 1 m from the fence and the fence is 3 m from the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach?
questions.explanation: The small triangle has base 1 m and height 1.5 m; the big one has base 1 + 3 = 4 m. So h = 1.5 × 4 = 6 m. Using 3 m for the base gives 4.5 m.
steps: Step 1: the triangles share the angle at the foot and both have right angles. The big base is 1 + 3 = 4 m.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you used 3 m as the big triangle's base. It runs from the foot of the ladder to the wall: 1 + 3 = 4 m.
mistakes.B: Step 2: you added 1.5 and 4. Multiply the fence height by the scale factor.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you divided the wrong way. The wall height must be more than the fence height.

questions.diagram_alt: A ladder touching the top of a 1.5 m fence and reaching height h on a wall. The foot is 1 m from the fence and the fence is 3 m from the wall

questions.prompt: A 1.8 m tall person stands 6 m from a 5.4 m lamp post (see the diagram). How long is the person's shadow, s?
steps: Step 1: small triangle: height 1.8, base s. Big triangle: height 5.4, base 6 + s. So s ÷ (6 + s) = 1.8 ÷ 5.4 = ⅓.

mistakes.A: Step 1: you used 6 m as the big triangle's base. The big base is 6 + s, from the post to the tip of the shadow.
mistakes.C: Step 3: 9 m is the whole base 6 + s. The question asks for s.

questions.diagram_alt: A 5.4 m lamp post and a 1.8 m person standing 6 m from it, with shadow s and a dashed line from the lamp past the head to the tip of the shadow

questions.prompt: A triangle with an area of 12 cm² is enlarged by scale factor 2.5. What is the area of the image?
questions.explanation: Areas scale by k² = 2.5² = 6.25, so the image has area 12 × 6.25 = 75 cm². 30 cm² uses k instead of k².

mistakes.B: Step 2: you multiplied the area by 2.5. Areas are multiplied by k² = 6.25.
mistakes.C: Step 2: you multiplied by 2.5³. Areas use k², not k³.
